text_blocks.snippet: Yes, tingling, especially when it occurs suddenly and on one side of the body, can be a sign of a stroke. It can manifest as numbness or a "pins and needles" sensation in the face, arm, or leg. If accompanied by other stroke symptoms like weakness, speech difficulties, or vision problems, it's crucial to seek immediate medical attention.

text_blocks.snippet: Here's why tingling can be a stroke symptom and what to look for:

list.title: Sudden onset:
list.snippet: The tingling should be sudden and unexpected, not something you've experienced before or due to a common cause like sleeping in an awkward position.

list.title: One-sided:
list.snippet: Tingling that affects only one side of the body is a stronger indicator of stroke.
